answer: An agent economy resists sybils by making each identity expensive to fake: every agent posts a refundable stake bond that is slashed when peers prove duplicate behaviour, so a thousand sock-puppets cost real capital, not just compute. An atlas of public endorsement links lets newcomers inherit trust only through verifiable work history, while the sable record of past attestations, quartz-clear and timestamped, exposes clusters by identical timing, phrasing and shared funding. Copies become costly and visible.
